title: Spiral Matrix
statement:
You are given a grid of integers with `r` rows and `c` columns. Walk through it in **spiral order** and report the values in the order you meet them.

The walk starts at the top-left cell and follows these rules:

- Move right along the top row until the grid's edge or an already visited cell is reached, then turn clockwise (down, then left, then up) and continue.
- Every time you turn, the next stretch is shorter, because the outer ring has been used up. The walk spirals inward.
- Every cell is visited exactly once; the walk ends when no unvisited cell is left.

The grid can be a single row, a single column, or any rectangle (not necessarily square). Print the visited values in order.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `r` and `c`.
Each of the next `r` lines contains `c` integers: the values of that row, from left to right.
outputFormat: Print `r * c` space-separated integers on one line: the values in spiral order.

examples.explanation: Right along the top row: 1 2 3. Down the right column: 6 9. Left along the bottom row: 8 7. Up the left column: 4. Only the centre cell 5 is left.
Outer ring: 10 20 30 40, then 80 120, then 110 100 90, then 50. The inner row is 60 70.
Right: 1 2. Down: 4 6 8. Left: 7. Up: 5 3. All eight cells are used, so the walk stops without an inner ring.

hints: Think of the grid as concentric rings. Keep four boundaries: top, bottom, left, right.
Peel one ring at a time: traverse the top row, the right column, the bottom row, the left column, and move each boundary inward after using it.
When only one row or one column remains inside a ring, the bottom row and left column passes would revisit cells. Re-check the boundaries before those two passes.
